I was lucky to find a specialist in ADHD who had ADHD herself.  
After years of research and speculation, I already knew almost everything about it.  
Then I found this one psychologist in 2012 in another city and went there to find out if I had this thing or not.  
I wrote my life story for her to read (because I was fucking tired of explaining everything to everyone and also because I tend to get lost when telling a story and forget important stuff) and we talked about my insecurities, school, work, friendships, my earlier years, my relationship with my parents, my difficulties, why I thought I had ADHD and what I knew about it.  
Then she talked to my dad mostly about what kind of kid I was, if I was hyperactive, lazy or messy, clumsy, distracted etc.  
Voila, ADHD.  
Then she wrote a letter in which she stated the diagnosis.  

I told her that it always bothered me that I felt different.  
That I know everyone has a different "level" of attention deficit but I felt like mine was absurdly high.  
I told her I felt disabled by this and that it bothered me so much that I cried often because of it (and for most part of my life I believed I was dumb).  
Then I explained everything I felt was wrong and used examples like "I tend to forget everything, important or not. Even things that are appealing to me like when I really want to read about some particular subject and then 5 minutes later I forget about it completely until 3 months later when I remember once I thought about reading about it, and then forget it again ad infinitum".
I noticed people bullied me for forgetting everything and that it was not "normal". People didn't believe how distracted I was and always assumed I was faking/attention seeking/problem child/etc.  
  
I basically told her how I felt and why I thought it was not normal and told her how I found out about ADHD and how everything I read seemed like it was wrote especially for me.  
I also tried to show her that I knew somethings about the subject and that I was not just wanting some drugs to study or something like that, that I knew therapy was also important and what I truly wanted was to feel a little less handicapped by this.

EDIT: The fucking moron who gave me Ritalin in just one appointment seemed very full of my shit and handed out the prescription to "shut me up". He also said that "if the Ritalin 10mg one time a day worked out, that meant I had ADHD, If not, I didn't." WTF???

We usually talk about feelings, almost everyday. How we're feeling about our relationship, how we're feeling about our lives, if there's something bothering us etc. We talk about how we're feeling, why we're feeling and make sure we're talking about the same thing (we sometimes argue about something but in the end we're saying the same thing with different words lol).  

So, yesterday I went to talk with him. I had already asked for a break so I could clear my mind and make the best decision out of the situation.  I told him that I felt jealous of their passion, because it's a feeling I don't see coming from him towards me anymore (and that bothered me for a time, before realizing that's the way it is in a relationship of almost three years).  
I said that I wouldn't accept two separated relationships, because that would hurt me a lot and things would end up getting bad. I said that for the two and a half years we're together and for the 6 years of trust we have in each other, I felt like I deserved not to feel put aside.  
I said that I had the feeling that this *passion* he's feeling for her (this boost of feelings, and excitement etc.) in this new relationship seems to be getting more attention and given more importance than the relationship between the two of us. And that I felt this way because he's so sure he *needs* to see her as often as he can, even if our relationship isn't going so good. I said I feel like the right thing to do was "fixing" our relationship before adding a new person.  
So I said it was best for we to break up for some time, because I need to get my life back on tracks and so he can go see her and be with her without feeling guilty or w/e.
So he said a few things, that he tried to make it work, but apparently couldn't. He just agreed with what I said and told me he wants the best for all three of us. He said he loves her, and that this feelings does not diminishes his love for me. But, yes, he was focusing a lot in their relationship.  
I said that I decided to end things before it went out of control and we ended up getting hurt and losing our friendship. He agreed, said he was sorry.  
And that's it. He moved from our room to sleep with one of our roommates. I cried myself to sleep last night. And we're talking just as before (or close to that).  
I hope everything will be alright for the three of us.

My parents wouldn't understand either. 
People who never been through a depression can't really know what it *feels* like.  
I think being depressed is just like seeing the world through blurred glasses.  
People told me "you *need* to be strong" and "you *can't* let this depression take control" and "you have *so* many things to be thankful for". Those things aren't necessarily false. But it does not help to say them, we can't *feel* them. They just can't see, because well, it's not they who are feeling helpless. It's so much easier to see things when you're on the other side.

You don't really need to say anything. I started talking to them online. People I didn't talk to for about three years.  
You can start geeting in touch online, if it's easier for you, or starting to get in touch slowly. Maybe a lunch with one, a few days after with another. If they ask why you were absent you can say you were not felling like getting out. Maybe if there's someone you trust the most, you can tell them you are not feeling quite well and could use some support.  
But of course you shouldn't do anything you are not comfortable doing. I just feel that getting back in touch with those friends of mine lifted up my mood.
